newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Airways to lock out workers.
newsitem.headline: S.African Airways to lock out workers.

text.p: South African Airways SAA.CN (SAA) said it would lock out aviation technicians and engineers from Wednesday if they failed to end a work-to-rule protest they began last week.
"Those members who have not indicated that they will resume their normal duties will face a lock-out," SAA spokeswoman Zelda Schuulabach said.
She said members would be given the chance to return to work on Wednesday if they signed a form showing they were willing to work.

Domestic and international flights at Johannesburg airport have been disrupted since some 3,000 members of the South African Aviation Engineering and Allied Union (SAAEAU) began their action on Wednesday last week.
Schuulaback said management and union members could not reach a settlement at a meeting on Tuesday.
She said SAA would have to resort to contingency plans including chartering aircraft and rescheduling flights, but that flights on most major routes would not be affected.

"The number of members who have indicated they will come back to work will enable us to continue to operate our most important routes, namely, Johannesburg-Durban, Johannesburg-Cape Town and to London and New York," she said.
Last week two flights to London and Miami from Johannesburg, which serves as SAA's technical operations hub, were delayed for about 15 hours overnight -- leaving hundreds of passengers stranded.

The SAAEAU union has declared a dispute with SAA for its refusal to offer a 25 percent wage rise. Schuulaback said management was willing to continue the mediation process but would not further discuss the requested pay hike.

"The matter of a 25 percent salary increase is not acceptable," she said. Management is offering a 10 percent wage hike plus a 20 percent productivity bonus which the union has refused, Schuulabach said.
SAAEAU officials could not be reached for comment.
